notes.title: v1.01 - Speedrunning fixes!
notes.content:
Hi folks! Just adding a few quality-of-life fixes requested by the speedrunning community that's popped up around this game. (The game now saves mouse sensitivity and volume settings, and I fixed a bug where the music wouldn't restart when you return to the main menu).

Any speedrunners out there, let me know if you think of other helpful fixes! I never know how much time I'll have to work on these older games, but I'll do my best to help out :)

Check out the runs here: https://www.speedrun.com/they_came_from_a_communist_planet#Any

notes.title: Have You Played… They Came From A Communist Planet?
notes.content:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time.

They Came From A Communist Planet

opens when you’re abducted from your miserable inner city room by aliens who tell you, among other things: “Capitalism offers no future. It can only seal off the exits.”

notes.title: Priceless Play 28 March 2020
notes.content:
Right. Well. It’s a bizarre situation we find ourselves in (and I do hope you are in), and I am here to provide you with your weekly dose of free games. I can’t deny that it’s rather surreal to turn on my video game machine (that’s my computer) and behave as though everything is some semblance of normal. While this routine remains the same, so many other things do not.

The games below the cut are a mishmash of things — games with peaceful meditations, games with poems, games to celebrate and bemoan being in isolation, and a rhythm game so difficult I might as well be Miles Teller in Whiplash.

Wherever you are, I hope you’re well, safe, and taking care of each other.

notes.title: This game is going to be free!
notes.content:
We're all stuck inside on Coronavirus lockdown, so what better time to play a game about taking to the streets? Consider this practice for after the quarantine lifts...

Thanks to everyone who purchased the game! Your support means the world to me :)

notes.title: Unknown Pleasures: Whatever a furlong is
notes.content:
There’s not long left before the big 20, but those crafty devs continue to release legions of games anyway, surely coveting the grand prize of a spot in the Unknown Pleasures annual finals. Or possibly they want to have enough money to buy food. Who can say?

Five more games join the ranks of the worthy today, for it is, once more, time for a selection of the finest under-appreciated games on Steam.

Doing that lungey thing sprinters do at the finish line this week: socialist revolution, cultist massacres, and pretty flowers.
